gen-dafont-junegull-gf-noto-sans-tagbanw: Junegull sets closed, pinched-mouth letters up top, with no thick-thin flicker, over the open curves and clear gaps of Noto Sans Tagbanwa. Tight shapes above, open ones below, make a clear handoff.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-noto-sans-tai-tha: Junegull traces every letter with one marker, cast-iron tall. Noto Sans Tai Tham follows with a crowded, chalk-board lowercase whose open c stays visible, so text would move along steadily.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-noto-sans-tai-vie: Junegull is retro and friendly, with closed, pinched letters. Noto Sans Tai Viet brings a tall x-height, short ascenders and pulled-back terminals, so open sans-serif shapes sit under the closed display ones.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-noto-sans-tamil-s: Rounded, parenthesis-like curves and a tall middle band make plain sans text look stocky next to the outlines of Junegull. Noto Sans Tamil Supplement stays open where Junegull closes up, and that push-pull is the main draw.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-noto-sans-zanabaz: Wide gaps and a soaring x-height keep this plain sans crisp at tiny sizes. Noto Sans Zanabazar Square stays open while Junegull's closed, one-width letters supply the retro punch.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-parkinsans: Junegull is retro, friendly and built tall, like cast-iron capitals. Parkinsans keeps one stroke thickness throughout, with wide-mouthed letters that stay crisp when shrunk, so paragraphs would run smoothly.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-preahvihear: Pinched and punchy: Junegull has no thick-thin flicker, while Preahvihear opens its letter mouths wide like a pried oyster. Aim the body a notch smaller; that lofty x-height carries it.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-puritan: Friendly and retro, Junegull draws its line as if with ruler and compass, no thick-thin flicker anywhere. Puritan brings rounded, side-open forms and oversized e and a counters, so text would flow comfortably.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-questrial: Junegull is retro and friendly, with pinched curve mouths and a lowercase as tall as cast-iron capitals. Questrial sans-serif text, with open c, e and s shapes and a stencil-cut flatness, would read cleanly.
